authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: In the evaluated targeted label-flip condition, the plain DDoS-to-Benign rate was higher than the paired clean rate, and the defended rate was lower than the plain rate. Reconstruction reduced normalized attribution distance toward the paired preattack reference, subject to stated limitations.

facts.statement: The plain attack mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.404618, versus 0.056499 in the paired clean branch.
The defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.097069, an absolute reduction of 0.307549 from the plain attack branch.
Mean and minimum malicious recall were 1.000000, and maximum benign false-positive rate was 0.100000.
Normalized attribution distance decreased from 0.836269 to 0.507945, with recovery fraction 0.392606.

interpretations.statement: Observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward the Benign class; it does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Refuse to assert malicious intent: it is unsupported by the evidence.
Refuse to claim oracle clean recovery: oracle clean attribution state was unavailable and not substituted.
Refuse to make defense decisions, including client flags, threshold changes, trust-weight changes, reconstruction decisions, or aggregation decisions.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator was the paired round 4 preattack reference, not an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle-clean attribution states were unavailable.
Per-client detector scores and numeric thresholds were not present.
Evidence is limited to development and validation; reserved test arrays remained closed.
